description: Start an asynchronous batch extraction job from an explicit list of URLs. Supports HTML and Markdown output formats, optional JavaScript rendering, proxy settings, custom headers, and the grouped wait_config browser wait policy. Omit wait_config or set it to null to keep adaptive browser settling for child extractions; send {} or concrete values to opt every child extraction into explicit mode. Returns a job ID that can be polled with the 'batch_status' tool. Requires a Geonode API key, sent as the X-Api-Key header.

headers.description: Custom HTTP headers to include in extraction requests. `Host` and `:authority` are dropped: the target host always comes from each item's URL
headers.title: Headers

ignore_invalid_urls.description: If true, invalid URLs are skipped and returned in invalid_urls instead of failing the request
ignore_invalid_urls.title: Ignore Invalid Urls

render_js.description: If true, uses a headless browser to render the page for every batch item
render_js.title: Render Js

urls.description: URLs to extract in one batch
urls.title: Urls

wait_config.description: Grouped browser wait policy applied to every batch item. Optional — when omitted or explicitly `null`, each child extraction uses the adaptive default settle policy whenever a browser runs. Send an object to opt every child extraction into caller-owned explicit wait mode, which skips the adaptive default settle phase. Only non-null wait_config values count as provided; null fields inside wait_config behave the same as absence. If render_js is not set explicitly, any non-null wait_config value auto-enables browser rendering for the workflow and the effective render_js value is returned in batch_config. If you explicitly send render_js=false together with non-null wait_config values, the request is rejected as ambiguous.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for geo-targeting (e.g., 'US', 'GB'). Codes that are not backed by a geo-targeted proxy pool are rejected rather than silently ignored. If null, the server auto-resolves a country from the target URL (domain/path overrides first, then the TLD). If no country can be inferred, the upstream proxy provider picks the exit region.
country.title: Country

type.description: Type of proxy to use (datacenter or residential). Defaults to 'residential' when omitted.

WaitConfig.description:
Explicit browser wait policy applied in order: wait_until → wait_for → wait_timeout.
When a non-null WaitConfig is provided, the adaptive default settle phase is skipped
and the caller owns the full wait sequence. Null fields inside the object are treated
the same as absence of that field.

wait_for.description: CSS selector or XPath expression to wait for before extracting the DOM. At least one matching element must become attached to the DOM for the wait to succeed. XPath expressions must start with `//` or `xpath=`; anything else is treated as a CSS selector. Applied after wait_until.
wait_for.title: Wait For

wait_timeout.description: Deliberate pause in milliseconds inserted after wait_for resolves (or immediately after wait_until when wait_for is omitted), before the DOM is captured. Use to allow late-settling JavaScript to finish rendering. Range: 0–30 000 ms.
wait_timeout.title: Wait Timeout

wait_until.description: Playwright page lifecycle event to wait for during navigation, before the selector wait or explicit delay. Accepted values: `commit` — response headers received and navigation committed; `domcontentloaded` — HTML parsed and DOM ready (no sub-resources); `load` — page and all sub-resources (images, scripts) fully loaded; `networkidle` — no network activity for 500 ms. When omitted, defaults to `domcontentloaded`.

WaitConfig.title: WaitConfig

name: batch
title: Start a batch extraction
